question: What mechanically constitutes a 'reaction' at a swept level, such that a level swept WITHOUT one is excluded from the draw set?
whyItMatters: CLAIM|TJR|20260727|011 makes the eligibility of every draw on liquidity conditional on whether a prior sweep 'produced a reaction', but no source defines reaction: no displacement threshold, no timeframe, no candle-count. This is the filter that decides which levels survive, so it gates targets, sweep detection and the leading-index test alike. It also carries a circularity risk: 'reaction' is close to the very thing the strategy's own confirmation step (CLAIM|TJR|20260727|012/013) exists to detect, so defining it without source support would silently invent the core of the strategy rather than extract it.
